# Introduction 

This document is the user-guide of the REST API for Outage Management. It includes the data model definition as well as all available operations for the Outage resource.

The Outage Management API provides a standardized mechanism for Outage management such as the creation, update, retrieval, import and export of a collection of outages. An Outage represents a record of a formally declared period of disruption or interruption of service(s) in a specific geographical region(s), preventing users from effectively accessing or utilizing the service. This could be planned or unplanned. It is comprised of attributes and associations which define all aspects known for a particular type of Outage.

The Outage management API will provide comprehensive outage details, including impacted services, regions affected, and the duration of the outage with estimated restoration times, allowing telecom operators to efficiently handle service disruptions for customers.

The Outage Management API manages the Outage resource:

- An Outage is comprised of attributes and associations which define all aspects known for a particular type of Outage.
- The main attributes are its impact, isPlanned, reason, state, estimatedDateToResolve, affectedService, affectedLocation and related incident or change request.
- An Outage follows a simple lifecycle which is presented later for illustrative purposes, defining such aspects as whether it is declared, restored or closed.

The Outage Management API performs the following operations on the Outage resource:

- Retrieval of a Outage or a collection of Outage, depending on filter criteria
- Partial update of a Outage or of a collection of Outage
- Creation of an Outage
- Deletion of an Outage

![](data:image/png;base64,)

# Sample Use Cases 

Once the Outage management system identifies an outage, it will generate an instance of the outage using the Outage Management API and publish API event notifications. The customer assurance component will then extract the necessary information from these notifications to inform customers via SMS, portal announcements, mobile apps, etc. This also allows MVNOs, partners, and government regulatory bodies to subscribe to notifications to manage interrupted services, respond to emergencies, and enforce regulatory compliance.

- UC1 - Declare Outage

    - Who: I’m an Outage Management component
    - When: I have received details of an unplanned or planned event, I need to declare an outage
    - What: I need to declare an outage as the unplanned or planned event is impacting customer service(s) and/or geographic areas
    - How: I will create an outage instance with the required attributes captured against the outage instance

- UC2 - Report on Outage instances

    - Who: I’m a Regulatory body, Partner, MVNO
    - When: On a need by basis
    - What: I require a list of outages during a period of time
    - How: I will query the Outage Management component to get all outage instances for a period of time

- UC3 - Subscribe to Outage notification

    - Who: I’m Customer Assurance, Partner, Regulatory, MVNO
    - When: There is an outage due to a planned or unplanned event
    - What: I want to be notified what is the impact of the outage and estimated restoration time as well as ongoing updates
    - How: I need to be able to subscribe to outage notifications from the Telco operator

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a CloudOutage and NetworkOutage inheriting properties from the abstract Outage entity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of Outage instances some may be instances of CloudOutage where other could be instances of NetworkOutage. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an OutageRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as CloudOutageRef or NetworkOutageRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

# STATE LIFECYCLE 

## Lifecycle of Outage

The following table provided outage state explanation. The state graphic gives an overview of the allowed state changes.

| State | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| initiated | This is an initial state of an outage and representsa suspected outage or planned outagescheduled. |
| cancelled | Outage cancelled as outage has been ruled out(e.g., it was a false alarm or no longer planned) |
| declared | Outage is occuring and must be declared. |
| partiallyRestored | A significant amount (e.g. at least half) ofservices/locations that were impacted have beenrestored |
| restored | All the services that were impacted have beenrestored |
| closed | Post outage analysis completed, and stepsidentified to prevent similar outages in the future |

**Field descriptions**

**Outage fields**

| affectedLocation | A RelatedPlaceRefOrValue. A list of the locations affected by theoutage. At least one of affectedService or affectedLocationshould be present. |
| --- | --- |
| affectedService | A ServiceRefOrValue. List of the services affected by the outage.At least one of affectedService or affectedLocation should bepresent. |
| creationDate | A DateTime. Indicates the time (as a date + time) at which theoutage was created. It indicates the time when an outageinstance is created after identifiying incident or change requestand recording suspected impact. |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| description | A String. A textual succinct description of the nature, symptoms,cause, or effect of the outage. |
| --- | --- |
| domain | A String. The network domain or technology context of theoutage, for example RAN, PON, OTN, Cloud, Cross-Domain etc. |
| estimatedDateToResolve | A DateTime. Indicates the estimated date (as a date + time) atwhich the outage will be resolved. That is, when all the affectedservice and/or locations are restored. |
| estimatedNextUpdate | A DateTime. The estimated time when next update will beprovided. |
| externalIdentifier | An ExternalIdentifier. External identifier of the outage instancethat is different to the current system. |
| href | A String. Hyperlink reference. |
| id | A String. Unique identifier. |
| impact | An ImpactType. Possible values for the impact of an Incident.ENUMERATED with values:\* extensive\* significant\* moderate\* minor |
| isPlanned | A Boolean. True if outage is planned. false if outage unplanned. |
| lastUpdate | A DateTime. Date and time of the last update of the Outage. |
| name | A String. The name of the outage. A concise string or identifierthat briefly distinguishes or categorizes the outage. |
| note | A Note. A list of comments or notes made on the outage. |
| outageType | A String. Describes the type of outage. |
| period | A TimePeriod. A period of time, either as a deadline(endDateTime only) a startDateTime only, or both. |
| reason | A String. A textual succinct description of the cause/reason forthe outage. |
| relatedEntity | A RelatedEntityRefOrValue. List of related entities associatedwith this outage. This could be cost, reporting managementtemplate etc. |
| relatedParty | A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef. List of parties or party rolesplaying a role within the outage. |
| restoredLocation | A RelatedPlaceRefOrValue. A list of the locations restored andno longer affected by the outage. |
| restoredService | A ServiceRefOrValue. List of the services restored and no longeraffected by the outage. |
| rootCauseChangeRequest | A ChangeRequestRef. List of change request(s) that areassociated to the outage. At least one ofrootCauseChangeRequest or rootCauseIncident should bepresent. |

## Notification Resource Models

### 4 notifications are defined for this API.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Notifications related to Outage:

- Create Event
- Delete Event
- Attribute Value Change Event
- State Change Event The notification structure for all notifications in this API follow the pattern depicted by the figure below. A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence (eventId), an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This notification structure owns an event payload structure ("SpecificEventPayload" placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

![](data:image/png;base64,)

_Figure 15 Notification Pattern_

# API OPERATIONS 

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| Operation on Entities | Uniform API Operation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrieve arepresentation of a resource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to create anew resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used to partiallyupdate a resource |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on an Entity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used to executeTask Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

## Operations on Outage

### Retrieves a Outage by ID

```
GET /outage/{id}?fields=…
```

**Description**

This operation retrieves an Outage entity. Attribute selection is enabled for all first level attributes. Filtering may be available depending on the compliance level supported by an implementation.

### List or find Outage objects

### GET /outage?fields=…

### Description

This operation list Outage entities. Attribute selection is enabled for all first level attributes. Filtering may be available depending on the compliance level supported by an implementation.

### Updates partially a Outage

### PATCH /outage/{id}?fields=…

### Description

### This operation allows partial updates of an Outage entity. Support of json/merge

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ( [http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub- resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| creationDate |  |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| lastUpdate |  |
| stateChangeDate |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| affectedLocation |  |
| affectedService |  |
| description |  |
| domain |  |
| estimatedDateToResolve |  |
| estimatedNextUpdate |  |
| externalIdentifier |  |
| impact |  |
| isPlanned |  |
| name |  |
| note |  |
| outageType |  |
| period |  |
| reason |  |
| relatedEntity |  |
| relatedParty |  |
| restoredLocation |  |
| restoredService |  |
| rootCauseChangeRequest |  |

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| rootCauseIncident |  |
| state |  |
| stateChangeReason |  |
| totalNumberOfLocationImpacted |  |
| totalNumberOfServiceImpacted |  |

# API NOTIFICATIONS 

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample REST notification POST calls.

It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in the REST Guidelines reproduced below.

## Register listener

**POST /hub**

**Description**

Sets the communication endpoint address the service instance must use to deliver information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.

**Request**

```
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
```

**Response**

```
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
{
    "id":"42",
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com",    "query":""
}
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Unregister listener

**DELETE /hub/{id}**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

**Request**

```
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
```

**Response**

```
204
```

## Publish Event to listener

**POST /client/listener**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.

Provides to a registered listener the description of the event that was raised. The /client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

**Request**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
    "event": {
        EVENT BODY    },
    "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"
}
```

**Response**

```
201
```

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST Design Guidelines.
